Fort Lauderdale
January 14, 1998

C. A. M. M., the Coalition Advocating Medical Marijuana, has launched a campaign to get a medical marijuana initiative on the state ballot in the fall. 

C.A.M.M. is a non-profit Florida organization formed to lobby for the "decriminalization" of medical marijuana.

"We have been working  diligently to lay the ground-work throughout Florida and unite those who support rational and humane laws," said Toni Leeman, President of C.A.M.M.

C.A.M.M.'s seeks to establish a right for individuals in Florida to obtain and use marijuana for specified medical purposes when certified as medically appropriate by a licensed physician. The bill protects physicians and third parties who recommend or provide medicinal marijuana and allows penalties for fraudulent certification or use.

Floridians for Medical Rights, a political committee of C.A.M.M., will seek to get the signatures of 435,000 registered Florida voters on their petition by August 1, 1998. With this accomplished, the initiative will be placed on the 1998 Florida ballot.

CAMM says can you help in several ways:
1. Become a member of the coalition -- join the over 3,000 voices in Florida calling for a change in the laws on medical marijuana.
2. Gather signatures for the petition -- be a volunteer.
3. Donate funds to the organization.
4. Write your Federal and State representatives and letters to your local newspaper stating that we need to stop putting sick and dying people in prison.

For more information please contact Toni Leeman--President of C.A.M.M.
